<thought>The spectrum shows a strong M+1 peak (~16.5% of the base) consistent with many 13C atoms, indicating carbon is present. An M+2 peak around 4.6% matches the natural abundance of 34S (~4.2%), indicating sulfur is present. No M+2 pattern matching chlorine (~33%) or bromine (~100%) is observed, so those elements cannot be definitively identified. Therefore the definitively identifiable elements are carbon and sulfur.</thought>
<final_answer>['C', 'S']</final_answer>
